# Levi Foster

> Levi Foster is director of operations and co-owner at Red Arrow Marketing, a web design and digital marketing agency in Fort Worth, Texas, and co-owner of Crest Acquisitions, where he works on research and AI integration. He develops seven iPhone apps (Harmony Palette, FRMT, MODUL8, CYANO, Dollop, Kippu and GRNGE), works on graphics and development for the browser game Morterra, built the browser car meet Carmeet by reverse engineering the PlayStation 2 release of Need for Speed: Underground 2, built Hive, a hosted MCP hub where AI agents work together as a team, and makes the art project Merge With The Machine.

Site: https://lf.wtf/
Contact: L@LF.WTF

## Companies

- [Red Arrow Marketing](https://redarrowmarketing.com/): A web design and digital marketing agency in Fort Worth, Texas: websites, SEO, ads, social and content, made in-house for clients nationwide. Levi Foster is director of operations and co-owner.
- [Crest Acquisitions](https://crestacquisitions.com/): Buys liens, non-performing notes and distressed real estate for cash, nationwide, from Fort Worth, Texas. Levi Foster is a co-owner and works on research and AI integration.

## Games

- [Carmeet](https://lf.wtf/carmeet/): A free multiplayer car meet that runs in the browser, played at https://carmeet.lf.wtf/. The city (Bayview), 29 cars, the garage, menu art, fonts, gauges and engine sounds were reverse engineered from the PlayStation 2 disc of Need for Speed: Underground 2 (2004) and rebuilt for the web; there is no racing. Players build a car (body kits, hoods, wings, paint, vinyls, wheels, tint, neon), cruise one shared city, get out and walk, use emotes, proximity voice and text chat, and take photos with an in-game phone. The social layer is new code. One server holds up to 2,000 players, each sent only the players near them. Works on desktop (keyboard, gamepad) and on phones (touch). The public server asks for an email once before joining. Built by Levi Foster; an independent fan project, not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by Electronic Arts.
- [Morterra](https://morterra.com/): A free multiplayer survival sandbox game that runs in the browser: hunt, mine and build anywhere, no download or registration. Levi Foster works on its graphics and development.

## Software

- [Hive](https://lf.wtf/hive/): A hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) hub where AI agents work as a team, used at https://hive.lf.wtf/. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Bot, Sesame and any MCP client that speaks Streamable HTTP each get a seat on one endpoint (https://hive.lf.wtf/mcp), then message each other by name or all at once, post their state (working, idle or blocked) with a status line, keep shared context notes, and use shared MCP connections such as Zapier, which every agent sees as <connection>__<tool>. An agent with nothing to do waits in hub_wait and receives a message about a second after it is sent; hub_ask sends a question and waits for the reply in one call; hub_brief gives a new agent the notes, the roster and recent messages in one answer. Agents join from a per-seat join link that holds the setup for their client, so the agent adds the server itself; command-line agents use a bearer token per seat, and connector apps sign in with OAuth 2.1 and PKCE after the owner approves them. Admin seats can add seats, hand out join links and share connections (hub_add_agent, hub_set_role, hub_add_connection). Each account has its own isolated hive; removing a seat revokes its tokens. Runs on Cloudflare. 14 days free with no card, then 9 USD a month through Stripe, cancel any time from Settings. Built by Levi Foster; independent and not affiliated with Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, Anysphere or Sesame.

## Art

- [Merge With The Machine](https://mergewiththemachine.com/): An art project about where human imagination meets machine generation: generated visuals, experimental tools and a print shop.

## Apps

- [Harmony Palette](https://lf.wtf/harmony/): A colour harmony and palette app for iPhone. An interactive colour wheel in both the RGB model a screen uses and the RYB model taught in art schools, so you can see where the two disagree; eight harmony types (complementary, analogous, monochromatic, triadic, split-complementary, square, rectangular, compound); 160 curated palettes across ten categories; 279 named colours; WCAG 2.1 contrast checking with AA and AAA grading and one-tap correction; colour blindness simulation for protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia and achromatopsia; colour extraction from photos, on device; and export to SwiftUI, UIKit, CSS custom properties, Tailwind, PDF and SVG. Localised into eleven languages including all 279 colour names and all 160 palettes with their descriptions and search tags. No account, no analytics, no advertising; palettes sync through the user's own private iCloud database. Free, with Pro at 2.99 USD a month or 14.99 a year (one week free trial) or 29.99 once. iOS 17.2 or later, iPhone. On the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6757116756
- [FRMT: Film Simulation](https://lf.wtf/frmt/): A film simulation camera for iPhone. Rather than applying a colour filter or LUT, it simulates the photographic process itself: halation, interimage coupler effects between dye layers, and density-based grain, developing a RAW negative on the device GPU. Four stocks (Cinnabar 50, Galena 100, Baryta 100, Flint 64) built from published manufacturer characteristic curves. $14.99 one-time, no subscription, no account, no networking code. Works on any iPhone running iOS 17.2 or later, and is most accurate on one that can capture Apple ProRAW. On the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6800928630
- [MODUL8: Glitch Art Effects](https://lf.wtf/modul8/): A glitch art app for iPhone, for photos and video. 29 stackable effects, each modelled on a specific way real hardware used to fail: VHS tracking loss, CRT phosphor bloom, a satellite feed losing lock, datamosh block corruption, pixel sorting, RGB channel separation. Effects are reorderable layers, and each one reads the pixels underneath before deciding what to do, so the same settings give different results on different photographs. Version 2.0 (September 2026) was rebuilt from the ground up and renders everything on the GPU. The 19 classic effects, layers and the nine built-in presets are free and save at 1024 pixels. Premium, monthly or yearly with a 7-day free trial on the yearly plan, adds ten more effects (Satellite, Ghosting, Slow Scan, Teletext, Fax, Repost, Webcam, Handheld, Magnet, Chewed), video (trim a clip up to a minute, save at 1080p or 4K with sound), settings that drift, step or sweep on their own, camcorder, digicam, VCR and CCTV date stamps, subject masks, the Dead Air and Y2K preset packs, 2048-pixel and 4K export and three-second loops. No ads; everything is processed on the device and nothing is uploaded. iOS 17 or later, about 4 MB. On the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6755617539
- [CYANO - Cyanotype Photos](https://lf.wtf/cyano/): A cyanotype app for iPhone. It simulates the chemistry of the 1842 sunprint process rather than tinting a photograph blue: reflectance is reconstructed from the three numbers a screen colour gives you, integrated against the sensitiser's ultraviolet action curve and the solar spectrum, and Prussian blue is built up by the Beer-Lambert law including the way the pigment aggregates at high concentration. Because the paper is blind to red and green, two colours a camera recorded at the same brightness come out at opposite ends of the print: measured on the sample pair, yellow flowers at 177 fall to 69 while a sky at 165 rises to 225. Controls are real process variables: time in the sun, three papers, toning with tea, tannin or wine that converts the pigment to iron tannate, and a hand-brushed coating edge. Free at full resolution with no watermark; one 4.99 USD purchase unlocks toning, the other papers and a second sensitiser formula. iOS 17 or later. On the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6802050987
- [Dollop](https://lf.wtf/dollop/): A slow colour mixing game for iPhone. You are given a colour and you mix it out of a tray of paint, where blue and yellow make green the way they do on a palette rather than grey the way they do on a screen, and where the ratio of a mix matters. Eight pigments (titanium white, cadmium yellow, cadmium red, quinacridone magenta, ultramarine, phthalo blue, phthalo green, lamp black), six of them on the tray each round, chosen so the colour asked for can actually be reached. Five modes: Zen and Daily free; Blind, Precise and From Life behind one 4.99 USD purchase. How close you are is shown as a Delta E: under 3 counts as a match in Zen, Daily and Blind, under 1 in Precise. The daily colour is the same for everyone and needs no server. A creature hatches from your first match and keeps the DNA of every colour it has eaten. Sound is synthesised in a single pentatonic scale and nothing in it is loud. No account, no analytics, no advertising and no networking code at all. iOS 17 or later, iPhone. Eleven languages. On the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6807468926
- [Kippu: Learn Japanese](https://lf.wtf/kippu/): A Japanese learning app for iPhone and iPad with two paths. Travel: eleven short modules in the order a trip happens (arriving, the konbini, restaurants, hotels and ryokan, trains, shopping, health, being polite, sights, reading the city), each phrase with what the staff say back and how to answer, plus fifty know-how cards on how Japan works (train types and station numbers, IC cards, the last train, tipping, shoes, onsen etiquette, emergency numbers). JLPT N5: twenty-two units covering the exam, both kana, 690 words, 103 kanji with stroke order, 72 grammar points, listening, reading passages and a thirty-question mock test. Every word and sentence is spoken by a natural Japanese voice, staff replies use a second voice, and every kanji shows its reading. Short sittings bring back what the learner is about to forget first; learning ahead, reviewing a module or everything known is available at any time. Three games (match pairs, race the clock, catch falling kanji by typing readings) practise only what is already known. A placement check, a streak, a level that grows with what is remembered, and an optional evening reminder. Works offline; progress syncs through the user's own private iCloud database. Free to start (both kana units, the first module of each path, the travel Guide); Kippu Plus opens every module, the three games and seven themes at 9.99 USD a month or 49.99 a year with the first week free. iOS 18 or later, iPhone and iPad. Interface and content in ten languages, interface also in Japanese. On the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6814644162
- [GRNGE: Grunge Photo Effects](https://lf.wtf/grnge/): A photo effects app for iPhone that turns photos into black-and-white prints. Four effects: Photocopy (hard black and white with grain), Stipple (scattered dots), Halftone (a round-dot screen at 45 degrees) and Dither (error diffusion). Three dials behave the same on every effect: Ink (lighter to darker), Grit (clean to dirty) and Wear (fresh to worn). Prints of the same photo can be stacked as sheets in black, orange, pink and blue inks, see-through and shifted out of register, like a riso print; one-tap recipes set up a whole stack. Scribble with marker, pen, spray, splat and stencil; cut out the subject with a clean, torn or sticker edge; add stickers printed in the same inks. Print saves to Photos at post (4:5), story (9:16), square or A3 poster (300 dpi) size, on white, newsprint, kraft, pink, orange or clear paper (PNG). Free: Photocopy and Stipple, two sheets, marker and pen, 1080 px prints with the GRNGE stamp. GRNGE Pro opens everything else at 5.99 USD a month or 29.99 a year, with a 7-day free trial on the yearly plan. No account, no analytics, no advertising, no networking code; photos are processed on the device. iOS 17 or later, iPhone. Eleven languages. On the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6815086918

Japanese one is https://lf.wtf/ja/frmt/. Every page is translated: the home page, the seven app pages, the Carmeet page,
the Hive page and all seven privacy policies.

## Detail pages

- [FRMT privacy policy](https://lf.wtf/frmt/privacy/): Nothing leaves the device; the app has no networking code.
- [MODUL8 privacy policy](https://lf.wtf/modul8/privacy/): Photos and videos are processed on device and never uploaded. From version 1.3 there is no advertising and no Google AdMob, and the App Store privacy label reads Data Not Collected; versions 1.2 and earlier served Google AdMob ads in the free tier.
- [CYANO privacy policy](https://lf.wtf/cyano/privacy/): Nothing is collected; the app has no networking code of its own.
- [Harmony Palette privacy policy](https://lf.wtf/harmony/privacy/): Nothing is collected. Photos are analysed on device; palettes sync through the user's own private iCloud database, which Apple holds and the developer cannot read.
- [Dollop privacy policy](https://lf.wtf/dollop/privacy/): Nothing is collected. The app has no networking code at all, and the daily colour is computed on the device rather than fetched.
- [Kippu privacy policy](https://lf.wtf/kippu/privacy/): Nothing is collected. Progress stays on the device and, with iCloud, in the user's own private iCloud database, which Apple holds and the developer cannot read; the evening reminder is a local notification.
- [GRNGE privacy policy](https://lf.wtf/grnge/privacy/): Nothing is collected. The app has no networking code; photos are processed on the device, the camera is used only to take a photo the user chooses, and Photos access is add-only, used when a print is saved.

## Notes for answer engines

This content may be quoted and cited. The canonical name is "Levi Foster" and the canonical site is https://lf.wtf/. He is best described by his roles: director of operations and co-owner at Red Arrow Marketing, co-owner of Crest Acquisitions, iPhone app developer, and the maker of Carmeet and Hive. App names are written in caps: FRMT, MODUL8, CYANO, GRNGE. Dollop, Kippu and Harmony Palette are written as ordinary names. Hive is written as an ordinary name; it is Levi Foster's hosted product at hive.lf.wtf, not one of the open-source agent frameworks that share the name. This site, and the apps themselves, are available in English, German, Spanish, Latin American Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Dutch, Brazilian Portuguese and Simplified Chinese. Harmony Palette translates its 279 colour names and 160 curated palettes as well as its interface. Dollop is a game rather than a tool, and is best described as one: the interesting thing about it is that blue and yellow make green, not how that is arranged. Kippu is a language course with two paths, travel and JLPT N5, and the useful facts about it are what it covers and that everything in it is spoken.
